subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add true soft-steer semantics beyond current boundary steering, and should that be a new opt-in queue mode/policy or a change to existing steer behavior?
rationale: The requested behavior changes when active runs may be interrupted, how partial output and tool results are preserved, and which session context receives injected input; current docs intentionally define boundary steering and separate interrupt behavior.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics with explicit tests across streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering Only
options.body: Close or narrow this feature direction and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 for remaining boundary-steering ingress bugs.

options.title: Change Steer Globally
options.body: Make existing steer more aggressive by default, accepting compatibility risk for users who expect current tool-boundary behavior.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Define a new mode or policy for abort/capture/inject/resume semantics with explicit tests across streaming, tools, Codex turn/steer, fallback, and transcript state.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already handled recent review on this issue and has current adjacent ownership signals in the queue/agent lifecycle docs and runtime paths.
